VibePascal v58 Win64 compiler -- a .ppu shorter than its own header says is truncated
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release: v57 (1f605f41b3b06a5fa84fb4cb31ee4298fb30907f)

       self-hosted Linux compiler 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076

Every other binary in bin/ is byte-identical to the v57 tarball.

The compiler reports its own build date as 2026/09/11, which is what
dist/win64-runtime-proof.sh stage 1 reconciles against the date in LATEST.txt.
The first v58 build of this same source did NOT: FPC takes that date from when
compiler/version.pas was last COMPILED, and an unchanged version.pas is not
recompiled just because the compiler is relinked, so a genuinely fresh binary
carried yesterday's date and the gate said so.  Rebuilt rather than papered
over -- a binary that misreports when it was built is exactly what that check
exists to catch, and the fix is to make the binary right, not the pointer
agree with it.

WHAT WAS BROKEN
---------------
This is the gap v57's own VERSION.txt declared under "NOT FIXED, AND NOT HIDDEN",
now closed.

v57 stopped the compiler HANGING on a half-written .ppu, but it only ever
noticed damage it happened to trip over.  Lose the TAIL of a unit file and there
was nothing to trip over: nothing an interface load reads lives in the last
handful of bytes, so the compiler read what it wanted, never reached the missing
part, and built your program against a unit that is not all there -- exit 0, no
message, nothing to search a log for.  Measured on a real 55291-byte unit, every
truncation from 55271 bytes upward was accepted.

A killed build, a full disk or an interrupted copy is exactly how a file loses
its tail, so this is the same accident v57 was about, landing a few bytes later.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE
--------------------
A .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete unit file is always
exactly 40 bytes of header plus that number, and can never be fewer.  Nothing
compared those two numbers.  The reader checked that the file was at least big
enough to hold the header and then trusted whatever followed.

WHAT CHANGED
------------
tppufile.readheader now compares the length the header declares against the
length the file actually has, and rejects it when the file is SHORT.  Longer than
declared stays legal, as it always was.  The arithmetic is 64-bit on purpose: the
declared size is an unsigned 32-bit field, and a corrupt header claiming near 4 GB
would wrap a 32-bit sum and turn the check into a no-op at exactly the moment it
is needed.

THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing:
  * if the unit's source is available, the unit is RECOMPILED and the build goes
    green -- measured, the .ppu comes back at its full length;
  * if a good copy of the same unit sits in a later -Fu directory, the compiler
    falls through to it and the build goes green -- also measured;
  * only a truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and
    it stops with the message an absent unit already gives.
Nobody is ever told to go and delete a file.

The other half of the change is that the length has to BE a length.  It came
from TCStream.Size, which is Seek(0,soFromEnd), and only a plain file answers
that with a byte count -- a range stream (a .ppu read from inside a package
file) answers with its last valid offset, one short, and an open-ended one with
a number that is not a length at all.  Left alone, that would have declared
every packaged unit truncated by exactly one byte.  So the length is now handed
in by whoever opens the stream and knows it.  TCRangeStream.Seek itself is NOT
touched: it works for the code that uses it, an open-ended range stream has no
real end to seek to, and moving its semantics to serve a reader that does not
need it is how one wrong behaviour becomes two.

UNTESTABLE HERE, AND SAID PLAINLY: no target in this compiler enables dynamic
packages -- the flag is tested in twelve places and set in none -- so a .pcp
package cannot be built to read back, and the package half above is written to
be correct if that is ever switched on rather than proven by running it.

VERIFIED
--------
  * 4000 real .ppu files in rtl/ and packages/: every one is exactly 40+declared
    bytes, so the check has no slack to fire falsely on
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh, extended this release to SCORE the tail offsets
    it used to document as an open gap:
        20/25 offsets clean, 5 problem(s), exit 1   on the pre-fix compiler
        25/25 offsets clean, 0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
    so the gate discriminates rather than describing
  * dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh x86_64-linux: 147/147 packages load clean
  * full 1983-test corpus A/B against a baseline rebuilt from this same source
    with the same command minus the patch: 1983 SAME, 0 DIFF
  * self-host fixpoint: stage1 == stage2 == stage3, byte-identical

WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64, with the published v57
exe as the control so the harness can still fail:

    v57 ppcx64.exe, unit truncated by 11 / 3 / 1 bytes  ->  exit 0, accepted
    v58 ppcx64.exe, same three                          ->  exit 1, rejected
    both, intact unit                                   ->  exit 0

The unit under test exists in exactly one directory with its source off every
search path, because a second copy or an available source would have let a
correct rejection end in a green build and read as a pass either way.

wine is NOT Windows: it is an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API
running the real shipped PE bytes, so this is execution evidence for the code we
generate, never a real-Windows sign-off.  Nobody has yet run any VibePascal
release on real Windows hardware.

COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY REFRESH on v57.  No PPU format, RTL or package change, so
THE UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin
tarball alone.
